report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is **true**. High-quality clinical evidence demonstrates that preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine-alcohol reduces the risk of surgical-site infection (SSI) following cesarean delivery compared with iodine-alcohol.

### Key Findings
1. **Clinical Trial Evidence:** A landmark randomized controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated 1,147 patients undergoing cesarean section. The study found that chlorhexidine–alcohol resulted in a significantly lower SSI rate compared to iodine–alcohol (4.0% vs. 7.3%, a 45% reduction in relative risk).
2. **Meta-Analyses:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses confirm that alcohol-based chlorhexidine is superior to iodine-based antiseptic solutions for preventing post-cesarean wound infections.
3. **Clinical Guidelines:** Major medical bodies, including the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), recommend alcohol-based chlorhexidine for preoperative skin preparation prior to cesarean delivery.

### Sources
- [New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048)
- [PubMed - Meta-Analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/)
- [ScienceDirect Review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282)
- [The ObG Project Summary](https://www.obgproject.com/2018/09/30/chlorhexidine-or-iodine-based-skin-prep-for-cesarean-sections/)
